citation: Sserhatt (repository), Argumentation Theory: TEI-XML Pilot Corpus for Arabic and Ottoman Debate Theory Manuscripts
title: Argumentation Theory: TEI-XML Pilot Corpus for Arabic and Ottoman Debate Theory Manuscripts
task_description: Corpus/resource for manuscript transcription, semantic annotation, and role-aware analysis of adab al-bahth wa-al-munazara texts.
inputs: Early-modern Arabic and Ottoman scholarly debate-theory manuscripts; TEI-XML witnesses, transcriptions, and line-level companion annotations.
outputs_or_labels: Role-oriented material explicitly discusses al-sā'il (inquirer), al-mu'allil (justifier), and objection order; repository provides *.annotated.tsv companions and TEI records.
pipeline_gap_filled: Disputation retrieval and role-aware argument skeleton extraction for an Arabic scholastic debate tradition.
artifact_access_status: public repository visible; exact files should be cloned and spot-checked before scoring
evidence_basis: Official repository README states five witnesses, TEI-XML encoding, annotated TSV companions, and role-based wording centered on inquirer/justifier/objection order. Source: https://github.com/Sserhatt/Argumentation-Theory
limitations: Not a peer-reviewed benchmark paper; no standard train/dev/test split or reported task metrics found; role labels are partly light semantic/editorial annotations rather than a fully adjudicated span-level gold standard.
why_relevant: Closest located resource to explicit scholastic disputation-role annotation: it is source-faithful Arabic/Ottoman debate theory and exposes role vocabulary that can seed a benchmark, while requiring validation of label granularity and reproducibility.

citation: Al-Sharafi et al. (2025), A Hybrid Annotation Model for Arabic Argumentative Debate Corpus
title: A Hybrid Annotation Model for Arabic Argumentative Debate Corpus
authors: Abdul Gabbar Al-Sharafi; Mohammad Majed Khader; Mohamed Ahmed; Mohamad Hamza Al-Sioufy; Wajdi Zaghouani; Ali Al-Zawqari
venue: Arabic Language Processing: From Theory to Practice (ICALP 2023 proceedings)
benchmark_or_resource_name: Arabic Argumentative Debate Corpus / hybrid annotation model
task_description: Annotates discourse segments in Arabic competitive debates with a hybrid Aristotle-plus-Toulmin scheme and evaluates annotation patterns.
inputs: Arabic competitive-debate transcripts from QatarDebate; discourse segments with speaker/topic/gender metadata.
outputs_or_labels: Position, super claim, claim, ground, warrant, evidential backing, rational backing, logos/ethos/pathos, plus self-repetition/team-repetition/reciting; annotation used seven trained native-Arabic annotators and double annotation for the first 20 debates.
pipeline_gap_filled: Attributed claims, premise/warrant structure, support and rebuttal-adjacent role classification in Arabic debate.
artifact_access_status: artifact/corpus access not independently verified from the publisher record
evidence_basis: Publisher abstract states the hybrid model, added labels, and corpus purpose. The published article evidence reports the label table and annotation process; source: https://squ.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/a-hybrid-annotation-model-forarabic-argumentative-debate-corpus/ . Additional accessible article evidence: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393128335_Arabic_Argumentation_Presentation_or_Proof
limitations: Competitive debate is not medieval scholastic disputation; labels are Toulmin/rhetorical rather than quaestio, sed contra, respondeo, or reply-to-objection roles; full artifact licensing/access remains unresolved.
why_relevant: Strong Arabic role-annotation comparator and a practical template for annotating claims, grounds, warrants, and rebuttal structure before adapting labels to scholastic categories.

citation: Visser et al. (2021), Annotating Argument Schemes
title: Annotating Argument Schemes
authors: Jelmer Visser; Floris Bex; John Lawrence; Chris Reed; Douglas Walton
task_description: Argument-scheme annotation and evaluation over televised political-debate argument structures.
inputs: US2016G1tv debate corpus with proposition/inference relations represented in AIF-compliant graphs.
outputs_or_labels: 491 of 505 inference relations receive one of 60 Walton scheme labels; companion Wagemans corpus assigns argument-type labels; original corpus supplies discourse structure and relations.
pipeline_gap_filled: Argument-form classification, support/attack/inference skeletons, and diagnostic evaluation of non-deductive reasoning.
artifact_access_status: corpus URL publicly identified; artifact should be checked at access time
license_status: Creative Commons 4.0 stated for the article; corpus-specific terms should be checked
evidence_basis: The article reports the public US2016G1tvWALTON and WAGEMANS corpora, AIF graph representation, 60 Walton scheme types, 491/505 classified inference relations, and agreement evaluation. Source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7888437/
limitations: English election debates, not scholastic texts; scheme labels encode inferential forms rather than historical disputation roles; no quaestio-stage or Latin/Arabic provenance.
why_relevant: Useful control for separating generic argument-form recognition from the harder scholastic role sequence and for testing graph recovery independently of historical genre.

citation: SCTA/LombardPress, Scholastic Texts and TEI-XML Editions
title: SCTA/LombardPress scholastic corpus and edition infrastructure
task_description: Machine-readable scholarly editions of medieval scholastic texts with stable identifiers, textual segmentation, witnesses, and TEI/XML encoding.
inputs: Medieval Latin scholastic editions and manuscript/print witnesses encoded in TEI/XML; example records include explicit Quaestio headings and source metadata.
outputs_or_labels: Explicit text/edition structures such as Quaestio headings, paragraph/line identifiers, witnesses, and editorial metadata; no verified gold labels for objection, sed contra, respondeo, or reply roles.
pipeline_gap_filled: Authentic source-text retrieval, provenance, witness alignment, and a foundation for future role annotation.
artifact_access_status: public repositories and APIs; exact corpus subset varies by project
license_status: record-level licenses vary; example record states CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
evidence_basis: SCTA describes connected datasets for scholastic research and corpus analysis. An SCTA TEI record exposes Quaestio headings, witness metadata, and a CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 availability statement. Sources: https://community.scta.info/ ; https://github.com/scta-texts/mm30o9/blob/master/mm30o9-d1e1345/cod-u78x10_mm30o9-d1e1345.xml
limitations: This is high-value Latin infrastructure but not an explicit disputation-role annotation benchmark; headings and textual conventions are not equivalent to adjudicated role labels.
why_relevant: Best Latin source layer found, but it must be paired with a new annotation pass for objections, authorities, sed contra, determination, and replies.

citation: Khader et al. (2024), Munazarat 1.0: A Corpus of Arabic Competitive Debates
title: Munazarat 1.0: A Corpus of Arabic Competitive Debates
authors: Mohammad M. Khader; AbdulGabbar Al-Sharafi; Mohamad Hamza Al-Sioufy; Wajdi Zaghouani; Ali Al-Zawqari
task_description: Arabic speech/debate corpus intended for argument-mining and Arabic NLP development.
inputs: Approximately 50 hours and 73 Arabic competitive debates, with transcripts and debate metadata.
outputs_or_labels: Transcripts, speech segmentation markers, and metadata; the corpus paper explicitly presents argument-scheme annotation as a future/use case rather than supplying scholastic role labels.
pipeline_gap_filled: Arabic debate-text retrieval and a raw-data control for testing whether a model can induce roles from unannotated text.
artifact_access_status: public repository and Zenodo record exist; Zenodo files are restricted
license_status: repository metadata public; files downloadable from repository per README
limitations: ACL paper describes 73 debates and transcription/review; the paper says the dataset can support future argument-scheme annotation. A later Arabic NLP paper explicitly contrasts it with the Arabic Argumentative Debate Corpus and states Munazarat lacks argumentative-structure annotations. Sources: https://aclanthology.org/2024.osact-1.3/ ; https://aclanthology.org/2025.arabicnlp-main.33.pdf ; https://github.com/moh72y/Munazarat1.0
why_relevant: No explicit objection/reply or argument-role gold labels; modern competitive debate is not scholastic disputation; Zenodo access is restricted.
confidence: Keep as a negative control only: it prevents conflating Arabic debate transcription with explicit role annotation.
